titulo: Evaluating for real: speed, turning and push
lead: A policy is only ready when it passes a test you wrote before looking at the result. In this lesson you evaluate the ready-made policy over 20 episodes with fixed seeds: speed error, turning and pushes of 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 m/s. Then you run your checkpoint from lesson 5 through the same test.
objetivo: evaluate a policy over 20 episodes with fixed seeds, measuring speed error and survival to pushes of increasing strength.

aprende.t: Speed error: 0.05 m/s between requested and measured
Fixed seeds: the same 20 episodes for any policy
Where evaluation in sim ends and sim2sim begins (course 2)

hero_alt: Humanoid robot standing in a dark lab, getting pushed from the side by a padded pole, taking a step to recover its balance.

secoes.sub: Click each block. avaliar.py runs all four in every episode.

nos.detalhe: Episode i uses seed i: same random command (vx between 0.3 and 1.0 m/s), same push direction. Two policies on the same test face exactly the same 20 episodes.
Average difference between the requested and the measured speed, only for runs that didn't fall. It measures whether the policy does what the command says.

With --giro, the command includes rotation. The ready-made policy's deploy.yaml declares a turn rate from −0.2 to 0.2 rad/s; in unitree_rl_lab's training code the curriculum only opens up linear velocity, and the turn rate stays at ±0.1 rad/s. 0.2 is already outside the trained range.

At 4 s, the base suddenly gets a horizontal velocity of N m/s, in a randomly drawn direction. unitree_rl_lab trains with pushes of up to ±0.5 m/s in x and y every 5 s; testing above that measures the margin.

secoes.legenda: The test is written before the result: number of episodes, command range, strength, and pass criterion (e.g., 18/20).

secoes.titulo: The ready-made policy in the test
secoes.sub: 20 episodes of 10 s, push of 1.0 m/s. Exits 0 when all survive.

blocos.conteudo:
F=${FTH:-$HOME/fth}; cd $F/locomocao && . $F/.venv/bin/activate
for e in 1.5 2.0; do python3 kit/avaliar.py --episodios 20 --empurrao $e | tail -1; done

abas.html:
política: unitree_rl_lab velocity v0 (ONNX) · 20 episódios de 10 s · giro +0.0 rad/s · empurrão de 1.0 m/s aos 4 s
erro médio de velocidade (quem não caiu): 0.05 m/s
sobreviveu: 20/20
saída: 0

20 out of 20 stayed up with a 1.0 m/s push, above the training (up to 0.5 m/s per axis, about 0.71 m/s on the diagonal), with an average velocity error of 0.05 m/s.

sobreviveu: 16/20
sobreviveu: 9/20

At 1.5 m/s, 16 out of 20; at 2.0 m/s, 9 out of 20. The margin runs out between 1.0 and 1.5 m/s. This kind of curve, not a single number, tells you how much the policy can take.

secoes.titulo: Your checkpoint in the same test
secoes.sub: avaliar.py accepts a .pt trained by the kit in place of the ready-made policy. Same seeds.

abas.html:
quedas: ep 0 em 1.3 s, ep 1 em 1.4 s, ep 2 em 1.4 s, ep 3 em 1.4 s, ep 4 em 1.3 s
sobreviveu: 0/5

0 out of 5, all falls before 1.5 s, even without a push. That is expected for 20 iterations: the test confirms what the curves already said. The value matters less than the habit: every policy, ready-made or yours, goes through the same test.

secoes.sub: What this test proves and what is left for course 2.

texto: That the policy tracks the command and withstands pushes in MuJoCo, with the Menagerie G1. The ready-made policy was trained in Isaac Lab: passing here is already a first sign of robustness.

That it walks on the robot. Different delay, actuator, friction, and mass are the subject of course 2, which measures this gap and runs the policy through a sim2sim gate with DDS before it touches the floor.
The concept of evaluating in simulation and of the reality gap, for manipulation policies, is in vla-v72, lesson 6.

secoes.sub: Write the criterion before seeing the number.

exercicios.texto: Write your pass criterion (e.g., 18/20) and only then run the evaluation with a push of 1.0 m/s.
Run 1.5 and 2.0 m/s and write down between which strengths the policy's margin runs out.
exercicios.pronto: the two lines show sobreviveu: 16/20 and sobreviveu: 9/20; you wrote "between 1.0 and 1.5 m/s".

exercicios.texto: Run the same test with --giro 0.2 and compare the velocity error with the straight-line one.
exercicios.pronto: python3 kit/avaliar.py --episodios 20 --giro 0.2 --empurrao 1.0 → the first line shows giro +0.2 rad/s and the last one sobreviveu: 20/20 (on 10/19/2026, error of 0.04 m/s).

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Why are the test seeds fixed?
opcoes: So the compared policies face exactly the same episodes.
Because MuJoCo does not accept random seeds when it runs several episodes in a row.
So the test runs faster on CPU.
So the policy memorizes the test episodes.
perguntas.explica: With different seeds, a difference from 16/20 to 18/20 could be just luck. Fixing them makes the comparison fair and repeatable.

perguntas.p: 20/20 at 1.0 m/s, 16/20 at 1.5, and 9/20 at 2.0. What does this show?
opcoes: That the policy has a factory defect with any push above 1.0 m/s.
That the margin runs out between 1.0 and 1.5 m/s, above the push used in training.
That the 1.0 m/s test was too easy and doesn't count.
That MuJoCo exaggerates pushes compared to Isaac Lab.
perguntas.explica: Training used pushes of up to 0.5 m/s per axis (about 0.71 m/s on the diagonal); withstanding 1.0 m/s is margin. The curve of increasing force tells you how far it goes.

perguntas.p: The policy passed 20/20 in MuJoCo. What is still missing before the robot?
opcoes: Nothing: two different physics engines already prove the robot.
Train again in MuJoCo to remove the dependence on Isaac Lab.
Measure and cover the gap, then pass the sim2sim gate from course 2.
Raise the push until it reaches 20/20 at 2.0 m/s.
perguntas.explica: Evaluating in sim proves the behavior in the simulator. The path to the ground, with the gap measured and a ladder of tests, is course 2.

itens.texto: Criterion written first, 20 episodes with fixed seeds, tracking and push.
The ready-made policy: 20/20 at 1.0 m/s, 16/20 at 1.5, 9/20 at 2.0.
Passing in sim is the first step; sim2sim and the gap are in course 2.
